summary: Phase 147K was authorized, following Phase 147J's AUTHORITY EVALUATION INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE COMPLETE verdict, to freeze the complete integration architecture into normative contracts. Produced AESIC-001 v1.0 -- Authority Evaluation Service Integration Contract, docs/contracts/AESIC-001-authority-evaluation-service-integration-contract.md, containing 117 sequential requirements (AESIC-REQ-001 through AESIC-REQ-117) across 24 sections. Froze the Authority Evaluation Service's (AES) public interface as a Session-object-only, constructor-injected shape (registry and aer_store collaborators; evaluate_stage_1/evaluate_stage_2 accepting only a Session object and, for Stage 2, a package_id), closing Phase 147J's identity-substitution and template-substitution hardening recommendation by construction rather than by discipline. Froze the Decision Template Resolution capability as an internal AES collaborator (never separately callable), its inputs/outputs/failure model/cache policy/versioning/retry semantics. Froze the abstract Authority Registry interaction contract (lookup behavior, version semantics, identity semantics, duplicate semantics, failure classifications, immutability, offline behavior, restart guarantees) with no implementation. Froze the two-stage evaluation lifecycle with Stage 2 unconditionally superseding Stage 1 for citation purposes, and the Authority Evaluation Record's (AER) identity, immutability, digest requirements, and prose-only shape, resolving Phase 147J's stage_1_outcome_ref open question as mandatory-when-a-Stage-1-outcome-exists. Froze a complete restart/replay matrix (thirteen restart points), a complete persistence contract distinguishing persistent/transient/recomputed/immutable state, a complete failure-ownership matrix (origin/owner/recovery-owner/user-visible-owner/logging-owner/retry-owner for thirteen named failure types), a complete outcome-consumption matrix with explicit authorization/permission/execution/policy-decision prohibitions, a complete security-requirements table (eleven threats, all contractual mitigations), a complete observability specification introducing a new evaluation_id correlation identifier resolving Phase 147J's third non-blocking observation, non-functional requirements (determinism, performance, restart tolerance, idempotency, availability, offline behavior, immutability, forward/backward compatibility, testability), and independent-verification requirements for a future 147L phase. Confirmed this contract requires zero amendments to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001, reconfirming Phase 147J's own determination unchanged. Overall Verdict: AUTHORITY EVALUATION INTEGRATION CONTRACT FROZEN. Full detail in docs/contracts/AESIC-001-authority-evaluation-service-integration-contract.md.
